title: 🛰️ Satellite 'TRISHNA' Sees Earth's Heat! India and France Launch a Thermal Eye Watching Water and Climate!
body: 🛰️ Satellite 'TRISHNA' Sees Earth's Heat! India and France Launch a Thermal Eye Watching Water and Climate!

The French ambassador to India announced that the TRISHNA satellite, a joint project between India and France, will launch soon, on a new mission to monitor the temperature of Earth's surface and its natural resources from space with unprecedented precision.

The satellite is being developed by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) together with the French space agency CNES, since it was announced in 2024. It is scheduled to launch in 2027 aboard a PSLV rocket from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre, and will operate for five years in a Sun-synchronous orbit at an altitude of 761 kilometres.

What sets TRISHNA apart is that it is a thermal imaging satellite using infrared rays, drawing a map of Earth's temperature with a resolution of up to 60 metres, and revisiting the same area several times a week, monitoring water stress in farmland, water evaporation, plant health, urban heat islands, and climate change over time.

France is building the thermal imaging instrument, while India provides the satellite platform and the optical sensor, in a cooperation that also extends to supporting India's Gaganyaan human spaceflight mission and forming joint working groups in space monitoring and space capabilities.

Experts say this precision in time and space will help scientists understand the world's water cycle, from plant stress to evaporation and climate change, which directly affects the food and water security of many countries.
Simply put: a thermal eye in the sky that sees the Earth's thirst before we do... Will satellites save the future of water and food?
Do you think monitoring Earth from space will change our daily lives?
